The byte-identical copy a project build writes into the build directory because declared outputs resolve against it (ADR-012 §1 addition 2, from the B1 spike's finding 6). The maintenance runbook (I3): what a contributor does when adding a concept, a surface, a journey, a document or a coverage claim, and what each gate asks of them when it refuses. Authored prose that points rather than restates — the subsystem guide owns how the system works, RELEASING.md owns the release cut, AGENTS.md owns the build commands — so it carries no inventory of its own to go stale.
Dated upstream review and release boundary with executable downstream adoption prompt.

Reader index of every concept s0ma teaches, rendered by the documentation application (D6) from the composed snapshot. Byte-gated by `s0ma docs check`; hand-edits are lost at the next compose.

Generated reference to every report s0ma can make (F3): each code's description and its severity in each of the four strictness modes, read from the canonical registries in `s0ma_dsl.config`. A build that stopped on a code can send a reader straight to its entry. Byte-gated by `s0ma docs check`.

Generated reference to both MCP servers (F4): every tool, resource and prompt each one serves, told apart by the adapter that read it, with what calling it does and which packaged documents mirror which resources. Byte-gated by `s0ma docs check`; hand-edits are lost at the next compose.

Generated reference to the distributions this workspace ships (F4): each one's version, license, purpose and in-workspace dependencies, read off the same `pyproject.toml` the component facts already name. Byte-gated by `s0ma docs check`; hand-edits are lost at the next compose.

Generated quick reference: every kind of declaration, every line each one may carry and whether it must be written, the words a line chooses from, the everyday commands and the basic rules, on one page. The human summary of this ledger. Moved out of plans/notes/ to docs/s0ma_src/ at beta-prep-5-front-door, because the ledger is a gate input — step 3 of adding a document, and three test modules read it — and a gate input must not live in a directory the public export withholds. Still a working record rather than shipped prose: the disposition enum, the audit's eight locations and the archive ledger.

The stability statement: what a pre-1.0 s0ma promises and what it does not — the invariants, the two frozen contracts, the schema-string discipline, what may change between releases (human-facing wording, report sentences, generated bytes, the served tool surface, studi0), how a project protects itself (its own toolchain, pinning, the committed-build equality gate), how a change is announced, which versions get fixes, and what beta means — pre-1.0, and nothing else. Names no version number. Authored at beta-prep-5-front-door B1; bound through the catalog and pinned by test_docs_guide_bindings.py.

Human-oriented troubleshooting FAQ (A7). Seeded from docs/hosting-getting-started.md §5 and the generated common_errors table, rewritten for people; defers the hosted channel's install/key failures to §5 rather than forking them, and says that channel is not the route the public repository offers.

The consolidated trust-model note (G7), closing the July GAP-1/API-5 gap: what s0ma treats as data rather than instruction, what each side-effect word means, how example and evidence execution is bounded, what the three connection surfaces expose and bind to, what the feedback flow can and cannot do, and the observed-versus-declared line. Every structural claim carries the gate or test that holds it; a consistency suite keeps those pointers resolvable.

Complete removal guide (A7). Covers a source install into a virtual environment, the keyed-installer layout and the Claude plugin or extension, and says which of those the public repository's first release offers.
